title: Flat affine section modules give flat stalk modules
statement: Let Y be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and G a quasi-coherent O_Y-module [pqf-def-coherent]. Suppose that for each affine open V of Y the section module G(V) is flat over O_Y(V), with scalars restricted along the equal-open appLE of the identity. For every point x of Y, the module-stalk functor [def-pc-module-stalk-functor] applied to G is flat over O_Y,x.

source.place: Tag 01U4, implication (2) to (1), specialized to the identity morphism; https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01U4

proof.text: Fix x and an affine neighbourhood V. The equal-open identity appLE is the identity, so the hypothesis makes G(V) flat over O(V). Restriction to V preserves quasi-coherence.

Identify V with Spec O(V). The quasi-coherent restricted module is the associated sheaf of its section module by the tilde-Gamma counit. Its stalk at x is the localization of G(V) at the prime corresponding to x, as an O_x-module; restriction to the neighbourhood does not change the stalk.

Under the preceding identifications put A=O(V), B=O_x and M=G(V), so G_x=B tensor_A M. For an injective map N to N-prime of B-modules, restriction of scalars remains injective and flatness of M makes N tensor_A M to N-prime tensor_A M injective. The balanced tensor associativity isomorphisms N tensor_B (B tensor_A M)=N tensor_A M identify these maps. The injective-map criterion for flatness gives flatness of G_x over B. This also handles zero modules and the empty scheme.

lean.statement:
theorem flat_stalk_of_affine_sections_flat {Y : Scheme.{u}} (G : Y.Modules)
    [SheafOfModules.IsQuasicoherent.{u} G]
    (hflat : ∀ V : Y.affineOpens,
      letI : Module Γ(Y, V.1) Γ(G, V.1) :=
        Module.compHom _ ((𝟙 Y : Y ⟶ Y).appLE V.1 V.1 (le_rfl)).hom
      Module.Flat (Γ(Y, V.1)) (Γ(G, V.1))) (x : Y) :
    Module.Flat (Y.presheaf.stalk x)
      ((RingedSpace.moduleStalkFunctor Y.toRingedSpace x).obj G)
